blocks.value: Just as stock prices rise when demand increases, they fall when more investors want to sell than buy.
Imagine This: A restaurant receives many complaints about poor food quality. Customers stop visiting, and profits fall. Investors lose confidence and begin selling their shares.
Poor financial results, bad news, weak management decisions, economic uncertainty, or market panic can all reduce demand for a company's shares.
If a company reports a major loss instead of profit, many investors may decide to sell, causing the share price to decline.
⚠️ A falling stock price doesn't always mean the company is bad. Sometimes the overall market is simply reacting to temporary events.

blocks.question: Stock prices generally fall when...
choices: More people want to sell than buy.
